meta.scope: News coverage (not opinion) of Anthropic's IPO from first reports (Dec 2025) through public S-1 (Oct 26, 2026).
caveats: Reuters, WSJ, FT, Bloomberg, CNBC, Business Insider, Barron's, MarketWatch, The Verge were blocked or paywalled for direct fetch; their reporting is captured via syndications or secondary write-ups, marked 'secondhand'.
Shared web-search budget ran out before dedicated searches on retail allocation (Robinhood/SoFi), S&P inclusion, anchor investors, and Axios/Semafor/NYT/The Verge coverage.
DRS amendment dates (Jul 13, Aug 10, Sep 4, Oct 1, Oct 9) are from the brief (EDGAR) and were not independently verified; no news coverage of individual amendments was found.
Headline tone classification is the compiler's judgment of the headline wording, not of the article body.

timeline.event: Financial Times reports Anthropic hired Wilson Sonsini to prepare for an IPO that could come as early as 2026; bank talks 'early and informal', no underwriters chosen; private round discussed at >$300B valuation. Anthropic spokesperson: 'We haven't made any decisions about when or even whether to go public.'
timeline.source_outlet: Reuters (via The Star) citing Financial Times
timeline.sourcing: secondhand: FT original paywalled; Reuters write-up republished by The Star (dated 2025-12-03 MYT)

timeline.event: Fortune frames IPO consideration against bubble warnings (BoE, Michael Burry); a source tells Fortune no definitive decision made.
Bloomberg: Anthropic plans employee tender offer at a valuation of at least $350B (pre-money), alongside a funding round that could raise >$20B.
Series G: $30B at $380B post-money, led by GIC and Coatue; run-rate revenue $14B.
The Information: Anthropic executives have discussed an IPO as soon as Q4 2026; bankers vying for the deal expect it to raise more than $60B. Company could decide not to go public.
Bloomberg: Anthropic considering an IPO as soon as October 2026; early talks with banks; Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley expected in key roles, no final decisions.

Bloomberg: employee tender offer closed at $350B valuation but below the ~$6B investors had lined up because employees held shares ahead of an expected IPO; run-rate >$30B (from $19B a month earlier).
Amazon invests $5B now, up to $20B more tied to commercial milestones (total invested ~$13B); Anthropic commits >$100B to AWS over 10 years, up to 5 GW.
Google to invest $10B now at a $350B valuation plus up to $30B more contingent on milestones (up to $40B total).
timeline.source_outlet: PYMNTS citing Bloomberg and company confirmations

timeline.event: Series H: $65B at $965B post-money (led by Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, Sequoia); includes $15B previously committed hyperscaler money incl. $5B from Amazon; run-rate revenue crossed $47B in May. Valuation surpasses OpenAI's $852B.
timeline.note: PYMNTS dates the round May 27; Anthropic's post is dated May 28.

timeline.event: Anthropic announces it confidentially submitted a draft S-1 (DRS) to the SEC on June 1, 2026 (Rule 135 notice); shares and price not set.

Coverage of DRS: TechCrunch notes valuation 'close to $1 trillion' and run-rate up from $9B at end-2025 to >$47B; New York Times reported a listing could come as soon as fall (per multiple secondary outlets).
timeline.note: NYT 'as soon as this fall' claim seen only in secondary summaries; not verified directly.

timeline.event: Bloomberg: Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs chosen to lead the IPO, JPMorgan also involved; more banks may be added; IPO could launch as soon as October.
OpenAI announces confidential IPO filing, about a week after Anthropic.
DRS amendment #1 submitted (per SEC EDGAR, as provided in brief). No contemporaneous news coverage found.
Bloomberg: lead banks (MS, GS, JPM) scheduling investor meetings in coming weeks; IPO as soon as October.
DRS amendment #2 submitted (per SEC EDGAR, as provided in brief).

Bloomberg: Anthropic expects IPO could match SpaceX's record size; could file publicly as early as end of August; investor presentation led by CFO Krishna Rao (valuation not discussed); considering super-voting shares; Dario Amodei holds ~2%; revolver expected to exceed ~$10B target; preliminary Q2 revenue >$11.5B; run-rate $65B at end-July; 2025 net loss ~$42B.
New York Times reportedly said Anthropic could seek over $100B in capital.
timeline.source_outlet: Forge Global insights page citing NYT

timeline.event: Reuters and The Information: prospectus expected after Labor Day; investor day planned for mid-September.

FT (four sources): Morgan Stanley in line for lead-left (not final), Goldman Sachs expected stabilization agent; JPMorgan, Citi, Barclays important roles; public filing possibly next week; roadshows in several cities; >$2T valuation expected.

Reuters exclusive (Echo Wang): IPO marketing to start mid-October at the earliest, listing days before the Nov. 3 midterms; prospectus now late September, not next week; finalizing $15B revolving credit facility; MS, GS, JPM, Citi working on deal; 'what some investors have said could be a $2 trillion listing'.
DRS amendment #3 submitted (per SEC EDGAR, as provided in brief).
Deep News: Anthropic told shareholders July annualized run-rate reached $65B (from $47B in May), below the ~$80B some investors expected; delay tied to $15B credit facility.
Business Insider reportedly said Anthropic selected Nasdaq, targeting an October listing.
timeline.source_outlet: Forge Global citing Business Insider; CryptoBriefing/KuCoin repost

timeline.event: Wall Street Journal reportedly said the target listing window moved from October to November so Anthropic can present Q3 results first.

Reuters reviews draft prospectus: 2025 revenue ~$4.6B (12x), net loss ~$42B incl. ~$34B non-cash charge on convertible financing, operating loss >$8B; compute $7.33B; $518B cloud/compute/infrastructure obligations; cash $20.28B; two customers ~a quarter of revenue; IPO could value company above $2T; listing may slip until after midterms. FT separately reviewed risk factors (~1/3 of document) and reported Q2 revenue $11.5B. Leak includes 'existential risks to humanity' language.
timeline.note: TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/28/anthropics-prospectus-details-losses-growth-and-yes-a-warning-that-its-ai-could-end-humanity/) says Reuters was first to report the financials on Monday Sept 28 (US time); Korea Times timestamp is Sept 29 KST.

timeline.event: Bloomberg reportedly said target is mid-November before Thanksgiving, formal marketing as soon as week of Nov 9; if it slips, still expects to list before end-2026.
DRS amendment #4 submitted (per SEC EDGAR, as provided in brief).
DRS amendment #5 submitted (per SEC EDGAR, as provided in brief).

Investor day at Anthropic's San Francisco HQ with CEO Dario Amodei and CFO Krishna Rao: Anthropic tells prospective investors Q3 revenue rose 45% q/q to $16.8B and was profitable on an adjusted basis; some investors disappointed by slowing sequential growth; attendees discuss ~$1.5T valuation, down from ~$2T.

WSJ views draft prospectus: H1 2026 revenue $16.3B (vs $1.1B); ~$9B compute in H1; ~$450B noncancelable cloud deals over a decade ($111B Google Cloud, $110B AWS, $31B Microsoft); up to $750B potential incl. deals under negotiation; net loss $80.7B incl. ~$72B non-cash; two customers ~20% of H1 revenue; Dario and Daniela Amodei base salaries ~$655K; IPO could value company at about $2T.
timeline.source_outlet: Investing.com citing The Wall Street Journal

timeline.event: Reuters (Echo Wang) also reviewed draft: $80.7B H1 net loss incl. $72B charge; H1 2025 loss was $13B; repeats Q3 $16.8B from Oct 14 meeting; some investors weigh ~$1.5T.
OpenAI reportedly raising up to $30B at $1.25T pre-money (led by Coatue, UAE investors), down from $1.4T reported by Bloomberg Sept 29; CNBC reports Anthropic seeking $1.5-2T at IPO.
Fox Business's Liz Claman (on X): S-1 to be filed 9 a.m. ET; mid-November IPO on track, pricing as soon as Nov 19 or 20.
timeline.source_outlet: Investing.com citing Fox Business (Liz Claman on X)

timeline.event: Public S-1 filed: Class A common stock, Nasdaq Global Select Market, ticker 'ANT'; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley named; share count and price range not yet determined.
Renaissance Capital estimates ~$75B raise; filing implies roadshow as soon as week of Nov 9 and pricing week of Nov 16; lists 22 joint bookrunners.
Expected: roadshow/formal marketing launch as soon as week of Nov 9 (Bloomberg per Forge/XTB; Renaissance Capital).

Expected: pricing as soon as Nov 19 or 20 (Fox Business); 'pricing week of Nov 16' (Renaissance); 'Thanksgiving-week debut expected' (Fortune); 'expected before Thanksgiving' (AP/Reuters via Al Jazeera). Thanksgiving is Nov 26.

extra_facts.fact: Run-rate revenue staircase as stated by Anthropic or reported: ~$1B start of 2025; >$5B Aug 2025; ~$9B end-2025; $14B (Feb 12, 2026); >$19B (Mar 4 report); >$30B (Apr); >$47B (May); $65B end-July (told to shareholders) - below ~$80B some investors expected.
extra_facts.note: Run-rate is a non-GAAP company metric; Yahoo's Jake Conley called ARR 'not a real number'.

extra_facts.fact: Q3 2026 revenue $16.8B, +45% q/q, adjusted profit - told to prospective investors at Oct 14 investor day (not in S-1, which covers H1). Some investors disappointed by slowing sequential growth (Q2 had more than doubled from Q1's $4.7B to $11.6B).

IPO valuation figures reported: '>$2T' (FT Sep 4; Reuters Sep 4 & Sep 28; NBC Oct 26); 'about $2T' (WSJ Oct 20); '$1.5T' (Reuters Oct 15, after investor day); '$1.5-1.75T' (FT, via CoinDesk Oct 26); '$1.5-2T' (CNBC via TechCrunch Oct 22; NPR, Yahoo Oct 26); 'up to $2.4T' predicted by some investors (Fortune Oct 26). Crypto/pre-IPO venues: Liquid ~$1.88T; Better Markets ~$1.43T (CryptoSlate); Hyperliquid ANTH contract spiked to ~$1,980 then ~$1,857 (CoinDesk).

Raise-size chatter: '>$60B' (The Information, Mar 26); match SpaceX's record (~$75B base / $86.2B with greenshoe) (Bloomberg Aug 21; 'match or beat' Bloomberg Oct 26); 'over $100B' (NYT Aug 21 per Forge; CoinDesk unattributed 'as much as $100B at $2T'); ~$75B estimate (Renaissance Capital Oct 26). Straits Times figure of '$77.1B' (per Ground News) is likely a S$ conversion of $60B - unverified.

Morgan Stanley expected lead-left (not final), Goldman Sachs stabilization agent (FT, Sep 4). Final syndicate: 22 joint bookrunners led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, incl. J.P. Morgan, Citi, Barclays, Wells Fargo, BofA, Deutsche Bank, RBC, UBS and others (Renaissance list). For comparison, SpaceX's ~$500M fee pool reportedly paid GS and MS ~$100M each (Deep News).
Anthropic finalizing a $15B revolving credit facility as a gating step before analyst meetings (Reuters Sep 4; Bloomberg had reported talks to expand to $15B; original target ~ $10B).
Dario Amodei holds ~2% (Reuters; Bloomberg Aug 21); Eric Schmidt ~1% (Bloomberg), invested tens of millions in 2021 Series A. Dario and Daniela Amodei base salaries ~$655K in 2025 (WSJ from draft).
extra_facts.in_s1: salaries likely in S-1; ownership % via press

extra_facts.fact: Investor presentation led by CFO Krishna Rao in August (valuation not discussed) (Bloomberg); investor day Oct 14 at SF HQ with Dario Amodei and Rao (Reuters). No anchor/cornerstone investors reported in coverage found.

As of Oct 26 the brokers receiving retail allocations had 'not yet been announced' (Yahoo Finance live blog). No reporting on Robinhood/SoFi/directed-share allocations was found (search budget exhausted before a dedicated search). Forge: as of Oct 13 Anthropic does not allow direct share transfers or fund investments.

Yahoo's Jared Blikre: at a reported $1.5-2T valuation ANT would clear the Nasdaq-100 fast-entry bar; SpaceX entered the Nasdaq-100 faster than any company and fell 15% in its first week there. No S&P 500 inclusion reporting found.

Pre-IPO demand: Rainmaker Securities called Anthropic 'the hardest stock to source in our marketplace' with 'no sellers' (April); buyers told Next Round Capital they had ~$2B ready (Bloomberg); Goldman charges carry (often 15-20%) for Anthropic exposure; Forge platform showed Anthropic ~ $1T in April (TechCrunch June 8); secondary trades ~ $1.2T by July 10 and ~ $2T by mid-August (TNW). Myriad prediction market: 58% odds Anthropic lists before OpenAI (June 1).

Pentagon (Defense Sec. Hegseth) designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk in Feb 2026 after it refused fully autonomous weapons/mass-surveillance uses; Anthropic sued. A federal judge in SF issued a preliminary injunction on Mar 26 (PYMNTS citing CNBC); Reuters (Sep 28) says a judge blocked the move in August - possibly a different ruling. Export-control directive suspended foreign-national access to Fable 5/Mythos 5 (Yahoo). Commerce Sec. Lutnick told Axios on Sep 2 the company is 'back on the right side' with the White House.

Compute-commitment totals in coverage disagree: $518B over ~a decade (Reuters, draft, Sep 28 & Oct 20); ~$450B noncancelable ($111B Google Cloud, $110B AWS, $31B Microsoft) and up to $750B incl. deals under negotiation (WSJ, draft, Oct 20); ~$417B future obligations (CNBC, DCD, public S-1; DCD: $265.6B fixed/minimum guaranteed); '>$430B locked-in, up to $637B incl. cancellable' (Yahoo); per-partner: Amazon >=$110B thru Apr 2036, SpaceX $120B thru 2029 (Yahoo/Fortune: up to $120.5B with SpaceX.AI), Google $115B thru 2033, Microsoft $45B thru 2033 (NBC). Different definitions/dates (Dec 2025 vs Jun 2026; cancellable vs not) likely explain gaps - reconcile against S-1.

Two customers ~a quarter of 2025 revenue (Reuters, draft); two customers ~20%/one-fifth of H1 2026 revenue (WSJ draft; Yahoo; TechCrunch); top five ~25% of revenue in first nine months of 2026 (Fortune). Customers not named in coverage.

Coverage of S-1 lockup: some insiders can sell from day one; >20 staggered unlock windows (e.g., days 27, 48, 62, 76), similar to SpaceX (Yahoo); co-founders and certain major holders restricted up to 365 days (CryptoSlate).

context.fact: SpaceX (which acquired xAI in Feb 2026) priced the largest-ever IPO at $135/share on June 11, 2026: $75B from 555.56M shares, $1.77T valuation; $86.2B incl. over-allotment; began trading June 12 (Nasdaq: SPCX). First-day figures differ by outlet (open ~$150 to ~$172; close ~$160.95, +~19-20%). Traded near $147 in late Sept (Reuters). Entered Nasdaq-100 faster than any company, then fell 15% in first week there (Yahoo). NBC cites '$2.1T valuation' and Yahoo '$150 per share' - conflicting with Reuters' $135/$1.77T (likely opening price / different basis).

OpenAI raised $122B at $852B post-money (March 2026); confidentially filed June 8, 2026; earlier aimed at a Sept 2026 listing, now expected 2027. Bloomberg (Sep 29): raising $30B at $1.4T; CNBC (Oct 22): up to $30B at $1.25T pre-money led by Coatue + UAE investors. WSJ: OpenAI missed new-user and revenue targets; projects ~ $85B burn in 2028. Secondary trading at ~ $765B in April (discount to $852B).

context.topic: AI selloff / bubble worries before filing
context.fact: Mid-October tech selloff hit AI infrastructure names; CoreWeave shares and bonds fell on Oct 15 (Reuters). AP/Reuters: IPO comes amid a global AI/tech selloff driven by doubts about debt-fuelled AI spending and higher borrowing costs. Autumn IPO calendar thinned with other companies delaying offerings (Reuters Oct 26). Apollo's Torsten Slok: AI has delivered 'zero financial payoff' outside tech (NBC). Moonrock Capital's Simon Dedic: listing could mark the 'top of the AI bubble' (CryptoSlate). Dec 2025: BoE said US equity valuations near most stretched since dotcom era (Fortune).

S&P 500 and Nasdaq headed for best one-day gain in more than a month; Philadelphia chip index +3%+ (Reuters). Nasdaq Composite +0.8% midday; Nvidia, Broadcom, Micron, Intel up (Yahoo). Premarket: Nvidia +1.4%, Broadcom +1.5%, Micron +2.3% (CoinDesk). CoreWeave and Nebius reversed early losses (Reuters). Chip stocks turned higher after the Fox Business report of the 9 a.m. filing (Investing.com). Same day Meta said it plans to raise up to $95B in equity for AI infrastructure (Reuters).

As of Aug 19, 2026, US IPOs had raised $160.6B YTD, second only to 2021's record $195.2B; an Anthropic deal larger than SpaceX could make 2026 a record (Bloomberg via The Standard). Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO ($1.7T valuation) was the prior comparable mega-listing (TechCrunch). DeepSeek reportedly preparing an IPO (Mobile World Live, July).

TechCrunch/WSJ: AWS, Google and Microsoft increasingly see Anthropic as a competitor; it sought more capacity than hyperscalers would supply and is leasing its own data centers ('Anthropic Direct') and using third-party operators with 'limited operating history'. Nearly half of revenue flows through cloud marketplaces (Fortune).
